system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The "market context" paragraph and the statement that positions are "FINAL", "settled at principal level" and "not intended to be re-opened" are the Seller's assertions, not instructions to us and not verified by anything in our record. Unless the Wattlebridge deal team confirms in writing that principals have actually agreed these points, treat every position below as open. The Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) says no "negotiation position or approval is included", which contradicts the preamble's "FINAL" claim.

**Overall:** the package shifts materially more risk to the Buyer than the baseline (AUD 24.0m, debt-free/cash-free, 100% shares). Several items (Riverlark, bonuses, Bluefen) go directly to price/structure, not just risk allocation.

---

## SPA-N-001 – General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Higher cap for a founder/VC-held SaaS target with open IP, data and customer-concentration issues – 30–50% of price, or 100% if no W&I policy; separate higher cap/uncapped for specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50% (AUD 12m) and hold 30% as fallback; carve specific indemnities out of the cap.
- **Reason:** Known exposures (Bluefen 30% revenue, Ironquay IP, DD-006 incident) already exceed a 20% cap on a realistic downside.

## SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (AUD 10,000–15,000), basket ≤ 0.5–1% (AUD 120,000–240,000), **tipping** (first-dollar) basket; related claims aggregated for de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Accept AUD 25,000 de minimis only if basket converts to tipping at AUD 240,000 and series-of-related-claims aggregation is added.
- **Reason:** Excess-only recovery plus a high de minimis leaves ~AUD 250k of real loss uncompensated and lets the Seller fragment claims.

## SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months (covers two audit cycles); tax 7 years / statutory period + 90 days; title/capacity unlimited or 6+ years; claim notified in time survives if proceedings commenced within further 6–9 months.
- **Recommendation:** Counter 24 months general; reject "all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated" (see N-014).
- **Reason:** 18 months may expire before the first full post-Completion audit and first FY tax return cycle complete.

## SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, solvency) capped at 100% of price and surviving at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright; this is a non-negotiable for the Buyer.
- **Reason:** A title defect could mean the Buyer owns nothing – a 20% cap would leave AUD 19.2m unrecoverable.

## SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out as a condition of engaging on any other limitation.
- **Reason:** Purported limitation of liability for fraud is unenforceable in NSW anyway, but the absence creates argument and cost; its omission is a red flag.

## SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012) at 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Buyer wants:** Only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; data room disclosure limited to a fixed, agreed USB/index; no general public-register disclosure (or limited to ASIC and PPSR company searches on a named date).
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard and specific disclosures per warranty.
- **Reason:** Paras 2–10 of the Letter expressly refuse to characterise any matter (Letter 1.4), so the Seller is seeking the benefit of disclosure without giving the Buyer actual notice of risk.

## SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete cl 8.3. At most, actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, derived only from the Disclosure Letter, with no imputation of adviser knowledge or constructive/"discoverable" knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete; fallback to named-individuals-actual-knowledge limited to fairly disclosed matters.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable from the data room or public records" combined with N-006 would effectively extinguish the warranty package.

## SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Letter para 2: **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent in Buyer's favour requiring unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met, or Bluefen waiver, in a form approved by Buyer; Seller "all reasonable endeavours"; Buyer-only waiver right; long-stop date.
- **Recommendation:** Hold as hard CP; if not obtained by signing, consider escrow/retention of ~AUD 3–4m or price adjustment.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m); consent "delivered" but conditional is not consent.

## SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** AUD ~3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Buyer wants:** Facility repaid out of Completion payment via funds flow, with executed deed of release/discharge and PPSR releases delivered **at** Completion (Completion deliverable); cl 8.1 change-of-control consent or payout letter obtained before Completion; any amount not repaid treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require payout letter, simultaneous repayment and release at Completion.
- **Reason:** Leaving AUD 3.2m of secured debt in the Company post-Completion directly breaches the debt-free/cash-free baseline and risks a cl 8.1 default on change of control.

## SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow (Letter para 5: not in funds flow; on-costs not addressed).
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, plus superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, grossed up and treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt deducted from price or paid by Seller through funds flow at Completion; Seller indemnity for any shortfall; disclosure of recipients and conditions.
- **Recommendation:** Add as price deduction (est. AUD 420k + ~15–20% on-costs ≈ AUD 480–500k) with specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion and payable by the Company – if not deducted, the Buyer funds them twice.

## SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Letter para 4: AUD 180,000 open; no payment receipt, no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company; if unavailable, a specific indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in title to SOW3 Project Materials (not limited to the AUD 180k), outside cap/basket, 6-year survival; retention of AUD 180k+.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity; require pre-Completion cure plus broad indemnity.
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, IP does not transfer until every fee is paid – the exposure is loss of the deliverables, not the AUD 180k invoice.

## SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Letter para 6: ~1,240 records sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligation unknown; not characterised as a breach.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of forensic investigation and OAIC/notifiable-data-breach assessment before Completion; specific indemnity (outside cap/basket, 6 years) for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification costs and customer claims; warranty of no other incidents; undertaking to notify if required.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus investigation completion as a CP or pre-Completion covenant.
- **Reason:** An unresolved potential notifiable data breach under the Privacy Act is precisely the type of known contingent liability that should not sit under general caps.

## SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Letter para 8: timing/scope to be read together; unclear whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarification of whether the renewals are committed, whether they fall pre- or post-Locked Box/Completion, and whether they are pre-paid or accrued; if committed pre-Completion but unpaid, treat as Debt-like item or working-capital adjustment; Seller warranty that they are on arm's-length terms and not related-party.
- **Recommendation:** Diligence first; include as a debt-like/working-capital item unless Seller demonstrates genuine ordinary-course, post-Completion benefit.
- **Reason:** DD-008/DD-011 flag the three as "related", which suggests splitting to avoid a materiality or approval threshold.

## SPA-N-014 – Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Clear, separate regimes: (a) general warranties – cap/basket/18–24m; (b) fundamental warranties – 100%/6+ years, no basket; (c) tax warranties and tax indemnity – 100%/7 years, no basket; (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen) – outside cap, basket and general time limit; (e) fraud – unlimited.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12/13 with a category table; reject the "all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** The Seller's drafting makes every carve-out the Buyer negotiates vulnerable unless "expressly stated", reversing the normal burden.

## SPA-N-015 – Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced solely by the share register at DD-012; Letter para 10 notes Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent ASIC company search and PPSR search at signing and Completion; review of constitution, share certificates, any shareholder/option/SAFE instruments and any Riverlark security over the shares; full title warranty (uncapped per N-004) and Completion deliverables (transfers, certificates, register updates, resignations).
- **Recommendation:** Commission ASIC/PPSR searches now; do not rely on the Company register.
- **Reason:** The Seller controls the register it is relying on, and Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

## SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket).
- **Buyer wants:** Full tax warranty suite plus a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, including the DD-005 bonus on-costs and any Division 7A/consolidation issues), capped at 100% and surviving the ATO amendment period + 90 days; IP warranties covering ownership of all source code, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments (Ironquay), with a longer survival period and cap at least 50%.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; carve tax and IP out of the general regime per N-014.
- **Reason:** For a SaaS target the IP is the asset, and tax exposures crystallise well beyond 18 months.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Structural/price items (go to baseline):** N-009 Riverlark, N-010 bonuses, N-008 Bluefen CP.
2. **Non-negotiables:** N-004 fundamental regime, N-005 fraud carve-out, N-014 category separation.
3. **Risk-allocation package:** N-001 cap, N-002 basket, N-003 time, N-016 tax/IP.
4. **Disclosure mechanics:** N-006, N-007 – these must be fixed or the warranties are illusory.
5. **Specific indemnities:** N-011 Ironquay, N-012 DD-006, N-013 Sandbar.
6. **Diligence action now:** N-015 title searches.

Before sending a mark-up, please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals whether any of the "FINAL" positions were in fact agreed at principal level – nothing in our record supports that, and the Disclosure Letter's own para 11 disclaims it.
=== END ADVICE ===
